instructions: The night before, or at least 3 hours ahead, heat the oven to 300°F. Cut 7 slices of the bread into 1-inch cubes, spread them on a baking sheet and bake for 10 to 15 minutes, until they feel dry on the outside but haven't browned. Turn the oven off.

While the bread dries, squeeze the 8 oz sausage out of its casings into a large skillet over medium high heat. Break it into small crumbles with a spatula and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until it's browned and there's no pink left. Spoon off the fat.
Finely dice the red pepper and thinly slice 2 of the green onions. Rub the 1 tbsp butter over the inside of an 8 by 8 inch baking dish.

Spread half the bread cubes in the dish. Scatter over half the sausage, half the pepper, half the green onions and 1 cup of the cheese. Repeat with the rest of the bread, sausage, pepper and green onions, and finish with the last 1 cup cheese.

In a bowl, whisk the 4 eggs, 1 1/2 cups milk, 1/2 tsp Italian seasoning, 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper until there are no streaks of white. Pour it evenly over the dish and press the bread down with a spatula so every cube gets wet. Cover with foil and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, put the covered dish straight into the cold oven and heat it to 350°F. Bake for 45 minutes.

Take the foil off and bake another 10 to 20 minutes, until it's puffed and golden on top. You're cooking it to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Push a knife into the center: it's done when it comes out clean, with no runny egg.
Let it rest for 10 minutes. Cut it any sooner and it falls apart. Cut it into 4 squares and serve it warm.
advance_prep_notes: Assemble it the night before, or at least 3 hours ahead, and refrigerate it overnight.
method_notes: Spend With Pennies (the lead) and Little Sweet Baker both layer dried bread cubes with cooked meat, peppers, green onion and cheese in a greased dish, pour over an egg and milk custard and chill it at least a few hours or overnight before baking at 350°F. Spend With Pennies uses Italian sausage, an Italian cheese blend and Italian seasoning and starts it in a cold oven under foil; Little Sweet Baker uses ham, cheddar, smoked gouda and Dijon. Natasha's Kitchen is a same-morning skillet version with grated potato, bacon and sour cream instead of bread. This one halves the lead into an 8 by 8 dish, keeps the crusts on, adds one more egg for a firmer set and takes the foil off for the end so the top browns.
